transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-19
Start time (PDT): 15:00
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Janelle Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Laura Benton (Harrington Head of Security), Samir Rao (Infra), Priya Nair (Compliance), Ethan Cole (DevOps), Oliver Grant (Procurement)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough): Intro to Redwood controls mapping, discussion of KMS integration options (customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed), trust portal access for auditors, SSO/SAML and SCIM user provisioning, and log export cadence.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we know it's a lot to cover so we'll try to hit your top questions — Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. Diego is our solutions engineer and Janelle is here for CSM follow-up.
[00:12] Laura Benton: Thanks, Maya. We got your invite. The two things I want to make sure we cover are: one, how we get evidence to the auditor with minimal lift; two, who holds the keys.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Totally. We'll start with a quick run through of options — hosted trust portal read-only exports, Dedicated capacity with evidence hooks, and our Private control plane where you keep keys — and then Diego will dive into the KMS flow.
[00:33] Diego Alvarez: Quick note, sorry if I mangle any internal terms, sometimes the auto-transcript turns K-V cache into, like, K-V cake, that was in another call, but i will try to be clear.
[00:40] Samir Rao: (laughs) we've seen that. Alright go ahead.
[00:44] Diego Alvarez: Okay so starting at a high level: our Trust Portal — we sometimes call it the 'trust center' internally — exposes artifact links for SOC 2 and ISO evidence. For hosted customers we provide time-stamped reports, control mappings and PDF exports. For Dedicated you get additional audit log streams and an S3-compatible evidence bucket that you can lock down. And for Private the control plane itself can run inside your VPC with a customer managed KMS so keys never leave your environment.
[01:12] Priya Nair: When you say "customer managed KMS" do you mean we create keys in our KMS and Redwood never sees them? Like full BYOK?
[01:20] Diego Alvarez: Yes, that's the BYOK scenario — you hold the root keys in, say, AWS KMS or a cloud HSM. We support a flow where Redwood is granted an envelope key use for encrypt/decrypt operations but the master key stays with you. We can also support an HSM-backed OIDC flow for the Private stack if you need FIPS/HSM assurances.
[01:41] Ethan Cole: For the evidence flow, will the auditor be able to log into a read-only view or do they need export files?
[01:48] Janelle Ortiz: Both options are available. We typically provide a read-only auditor role with limited Trust Portal access plus an evidence export (signed manifests in S3) that you can hand over. For Private installs that can run in your network, you can restrict the auditor's access to a jump host or provide exports only.
[02:05] Laura Benton: We prefer not to give external auditors any inbound access to our VPC. So exports are preferred. Retention windows: we need retention of raw audit logs for 2 years and control artifacts for 7 years, is that configurable?
[02:18] Diego Alvarez: Yes, retention on exported logs is configurable. Our hosted defaults are 90 days for high-fidelity audit streams but you can configure longer retention or set up automatic exports to your S3 with lifecycle policies. For Dedicated and Private you can set retention to meet your 2/7 year needs — though storage will be priced accordingly. We'll include that in the pilot pricing.
[02:36] Samir Rao: Is the audit log schema documented? We need field names — like request_id, principal, model_name, input_size, response_tokens — things our SIEM ingests.
[02:45] Diego Alvarez: Yep, there's a schema doc. I'll share the schema CSV. A heads up: some internal field names in the schema file might differ from what the transcript picks up — e.g., "req_id" vs "requestId" — but the docs have examples.
[02:56] Priya Nair: For SOC 2 evidence, do you map controls to the evidence artifacts? Or do we have to do the mapping?
[03:02] Maya Chen: We provide a control mapping CSV that maps Redwood controls to common SOC 2 / ISO clauses. It's a living document; for enterprise customers we can augment with your internal control IDs. Diego will share a sample.
[03:12] Oliver Grant: Any concerns about data residency? Our corp policy requires that all production inference data for EU clients stays in eu-west-1 and cannot be mirrored outside.
[03:20] Diego Alvarez: We support region pinning. For hosted customers we can pin to eu-west-1 for your EU workload; for Dedicated and Private you can isolate completely. One nuance: backups of logs can be cross-region unless you explicitly disable cross-region backups in the config — we'll show that in the pilot.
[03:36] Laura Benton: Can you describe the RBAC model? We have dozens of teams and need role scoping and least privilege for auditors vs ops vs engineers.
[03:45] Diego Alvarez: Sure — our platform uses role-based policies with resource scoping. Out of the box we have roles like admin, auditor-readonly, devops, and model-ops. We support SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO so you can automate group-to-role mapping. Note: SCIM is available for Dedicated and Private; hosted supports SAML + manual group sync today.
[04:05] Ethan Cole: We're using Okta — any quirks?
[04:08] Diego Alvarez: Okta is common. We have an Okta integration guide that covers SAML and SCIM. One small caveat: if you use SCIM for group sync, make sure the Okta group names align to the role names we expect — otherwise mappings need to be adjusted manually.
[04:22] Laura Benton: For encryption, do we get field-level encryption for embeddings or is it whole-volume?
[04:27] Diego Alvarez: Current model is at-rest encryption and envelope encryption for objects. Field-level encryption for in-flight tensors isn't something we expose to customers at the moment — most customers use envelope encryption + strict KMS policies. If you need additional application-level encryption we can discuss implementation patterns.
[04:40] Samir Rao: Audit log export frequency — is it near real-time or batch? We want near real-time to feed SIEM for anomaly detections.
[04:47] Diego Alvarez: We can stream to your Kinesis or Pub/Sub close to real-time, or push a batch S3 export every hour. Near real-time streaming is part of Dedicated/Private plans; hosted has a streaming add-on. We'll include the streaming throughput numbers in the doc.
[05:00] Laura Benton: On the SOC 2 report side — do you give us the auditor's report or just the summary? We need the actual auditor attestation for our vendor risk team.
[05:08] Maya Chen: We can provide the SOC 2 Type II report and the management assertion PDF. For customers under NDA we can provide deeper artifacts on a per-request basis. We don't publish raw auditor working papers though.
[05:18] Priya Nair: If we run Private, what's the upgrade path? Do we get patch notes and timelines? Who manages patching?
[05:26] Janelle Ortiz: For Private installs, Redwood provides release artifacts and a patch timeline. Patching can be performed by your ops team with our guidance or by Redwood under a managed ticket. For audited customers we typically do a change freeze window aligned with your audit schedule.
[05:40] Samir Rao: There's a security question: can we maintain a cryptographic audit trail linking evidence artifacts to an immutable ledger? We need non-repudiation for some controls.
[05:50] Diego Alvarez: We support signed manifests and object immutability via S3 Object Lock in compliance mode if your storage supports it. That pattern is used by several financial customers.
[06:02] Laura Benton: Alright let's surface open items — who will own what for the pilot?
[06:07] Maya Chen: From Redwood side, Diego will share the mapping and schema; I'll share pricing and pilot SLOs; Janelle will coordinate the onboarding timeline. From Harrington, Priya will confirm auditor contacts and retention windows; Samir/Ethan will provide allowlist and test VPC details; Oliver will coordinate procurement terms.
[06:25] Oliver Grant: Procurement will need an example MSA and a data processing addendum for our legal team.
[06:30] Maya Chen: Noted — we'll attach an MSA template and DPA in the follow-up.
[06:33] Priya Nair: One last clarifying Q: log field granularity — do you include prompt text in logs by default or is that redacted? This is a big privacy ask.
[06:44] Diego Alvarez: By default, we include input and output tokens in the audit stream but you can configure redaction or token hashing. For PI-sensitive workloads customers often configure upstream redaction or only capture metadata and hashes. We'll include redaction options in the controls mapping doc.
[06:58] Laura Benton: Good. Thank you.
[07:00] Maya Chen: Great. We'll summarize next steps in email. Any final quick questions?
[07:06] Priya Nair: No, just please include the retention pricing assumptions.
[07:09] Maya Chen: Will do. Thanks everyone.
